title: Refactor deploy drops a caching decorator, sending 12x read load to the database
source_note: Failure pattern (a deploy that inadvertently removes caching so a hot path hits the database on every request, spiking DB load and latency) is a recurring class in the danluu/post-mortems collection. All services, commit hashes, log lines, metrics, and timestamps are fabricated for evaluation.
incident_report: Since ~10:23 UTC product pages are very slow and some are timing out. A refactor of product-api went out around 10:20. Database team says product-api read load is way up.

signal_lines.msg: product-api e4f5a6b deployed to all hosts (product detail assembly refactor)
product detail cache hit rate dropped from 94% to 3%
read query volume from product-api up ~12x; read latency rising
p95 latency 3200ms (baseline ~180ms); ~4% of requests timing out
product-api rolled back; cache hit rate and latency recovering

ground_truth.root_cause: Deploy e4f5a6b refactored the product-detail assembly path and removed the caching decorator around the per-product lookup. Requests that previously served from cache (94% hit rate) now made a fresh database query per product, raising product-api's database read volume ~12x. The database could not keep up, so p95 latency climbed to ~3.2s and ~4% of requests timed out. Recovery on rollback.
evidence_path: deploy e4f5a6b to product-api at 10:20 (product detail assembly refactor)
product-api cache hit rate collapses from 94% to 3% immediately after the deploy
product-api p95 latency climbs to ~3.2s with ~4% timeouts
cache hit rate and latency recover on rollback
ground_truth.fix: Roll back e4f5a6b (done). Re-apply the refactor with the cache decorator restored, add a test asserting the product-detail path stays cached, and alert on a sudden cache-hit-rate drop.
